findings.description: The trigger requires detection when execution has not completed at the limit, while the same statement exempts completion at that instant. CON-SUP-103 specifies both an overrun longer than the limit and detection at expiry; OP-SYS-008 records the unresolved boundary and detection instant.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the expiry and simultaneous-completion semantics with the source owner, then state one consistent trigger and detection time.

findings.description: After a reset that preserves a latched safe state, a fault-free control cycle can satisfy the stated refresh condition, but SYS-SUP-043 prohibits refreshing while the safe state is latched. CON-SUP-110 requires the latch to survive software and watchdog resets.
findings.requested_change: Align the scheduled refresh condition with the latch and fault conditions in SYS-SUP-043.

findings.description: The statement restricts when the independent watchdog may be refreshed but never requires a refresh while healthy. An implementation that never refreshes it would satisfy this statement, although STK-SUP-005 calls for servicing the watchdogs and CON-SUP-106 specifies a 100 ms timeout.
findings.requested_change: Specify the required independent-watchdog servicing behavior and timing under the permitted healthy conditions, using an agreed source or recorded derivation.

findings.description: CON-SUP-107 supplies the CRC polynomial, but OP-SYS-010 identifies missing parameters and data-range details. The stated test cannot uniquely determine the expected CRC or whether the verification is correct.
findings.requested_change: Obtain and reference a complete CRC definition and the covered data and stored-value representation.

findings.description: The reset obligation is triggered only after the fault report has been transmitted. If transmission has not completed within 20 ms of entering the safe state, the statement imposes no reset request by the deadline, whereas CON-SUP-110 requires the report followed by a reset request within that interval.
findings.requested_change: Define the required reset sequence and deadline from safe-state entry without making the deadline conditional on a potentially late transmission; resolve any infeasible timing with the source owner.

findings.description: Retention of the safe-state latch and retention of the fault history across resets are independently judgeable: either can be lost while the other is retained. CON-SUP-110 requires both.
findings.requested_change: Split latch retention and fault-history retention into independently verifiable obligations.

findings.description: After the checks pass and the stated conditions hold, the requirement to drive the status signal high has no response time. CON-SUP-109 identifies high as operational, but the item gives no measurable point by which that indication must appear.
findings.requested_change: Define a source-supported response time or precise event for asserting the operational status, or record the missing decision as an open point.

findings.description: The trigger applies to every GET FAULTS request and requires eight reports even when fewer exist; SYS-SUP-044 explicitly establishes an empty history after power restoration. OP-SYS-011 records that CON-SUP-113 does not define the response for fewer than eight retained reports.
findings.requested_change: Limit the eight-report obligation to the applicable retained-history condition and specify the response for zero to seven reports once the source owner decides it.

findings.description: CON-SUP-116 says fault-injection hooks exist only in test builds. The statement requires hooks in test builds but does not prohibit them in other builds, so it does not express that source constraint.
findings.requested_change: Add an independently verifiable obligation that the fault-injection hooks exist only in test builds.

findings.description: Clearing the safe-state latch and emptying fault history after restored power are independently judgeable outcomes: one can succeed while the other fails. Both are addressed by CON-SUP-110.
findings.requested_change: Split the post-power-loss latch and fault-history outcomes into independently verifiable obligations.
